title: Morpheus v1: authorship, bioelectric coupling and audited self-improvement in regenerating synthetic tissues
status: Committed to the repository before any confirmatory run. Pilot runs used only an early 120-iteration rule that is not analysed, to debug the pipeline.
scope: Synthetic computational experiments on a neural cellular automaton. Nothing here measures or implies sentience, consciousness or biological validity. 'Self-model' names a trained forward model inside each cell, and nothing more.
units: One unit is a tissue: a founder cell grown under a frozen evolved rule, one wound drawn from the preregistered wound suite, and one stream of asynchronous-update noise. Every condition within an experiment reuses the same founders, wounds and noise (paired design, common random numbers).

rules.A: weights/rule_a.json: trained by backpropagation through time, seed 0, 2000 iterations, batch 16 (see weights meta). Primary.
rules.B: weights/rule_b.json: identical recipe, seed 1. Replication. The analysis of rule B is identical and was fixed before rule B was trained.

training_is_not_a_test: Training uses only random wounds from generator seeds drawn inside train_bptt; confirmatory suites use fixed seeds 1-4 and 10000+/20000+/30000+ that the trainer never draws from.

H1.claim: Authorship: a regenerating tissue whose comparator receives its own self-model error regenerates better than when its comparator receives another tissue's error stream (transplant).
H1.measure: regeneration loss (mean over the last 8 of 48 regeneration steps of the anatomical MSE); per-tissue difference transplant minus author
H1.test: one-sided sign-flip permutation test on the mean paired difference, alpha 0.05, plus bootstrap 95% CI
H1.support_rule: p < 0.05 and the CI lower bound > 0
H1.secondary: zero, delayed (8 steps) and shuffled (own error, permuted across the tissue's cells) versus author; Holm correction across the four contrasts including transplant
H1.descriptive: R^2 of the comparator input from the receiving cell's own 13-channel state, per condition (the Ghost-in-the-Machine v7 analogue: is an author's error its own?)

H2.claim: Gap junctions: blocking voltage coupling (diffusion = 0) during regeneration increases regeneration loss.
H2.measure: regeneration loss; per-tissue difference blocked minus normal
H2.test: one-sided sign-flip permutation, alpha 0.05, bootstrap CI

H3.claim: Bioelectric memory: after a head amputation, clamping every cell's voltage for 12 steps to the value grown tissues show in their tail region (v*, measured on a separate calibration suite, seed 99) changes the regenerated anatomy (H3a), and the change persists through a second head amputation with no clamp (H3b).
H3.measure: regeneration loss after the first and after the second regeneration (48 steps each); per-tissue difference pulse minus control
H3.test: two-sided sign-flip permutation, alpha 0.05 each; H3b is interpreted only if H3a is supported
H3.descriptive: anterior identity index: in the target head region, fraction of cells typed head minus fraction typed tail

CAL.claim: Null calibration of the H1 pipeline: A/A comparisons (author vs author with different update noise) reject at about the nominal rate.
CAL.expectation: false-positive rate at 0.05 not significantly above 0.05 (binomial)

H4.claim: Audited self-improvement: with the same proposer, a naive loop (adopt when a reused 8-tissue benchmark improves) overstates its own progress more than a gated loop (fresh 24 tissues per decision, sign-flip p against a LORD++ online-FDR level at alpha 0.1, plus a frozen 16-tissue anchor with 2% tolerance).
H4.measure: self-deception = believed cumulative gain (sum of estimates at adoption) minus true gain (test-suite loss before minus after, 128 held-out tissues never used for decisions)
H4.test: paired by loop seed (6 seeds, 40 proposals each), one-sided exact sign-flip on naive minus gated self-deception, alpha 0.05
H4.secondary: false adoptions (adopted edits whose true test gain <= 0), true gain, number adopted; descriptive only

deviations: Any deviation from this file is listed in docs/DEVIATIONS.md with its reason. Results files record the SHA-256 of this file.
